summary:
We created a beautiful and well-designed web application, SPHEREx Explorer, which is developed using React and FastAPI. It helps NASA's next infrared sky surveys to be explored by scientists, students, and space enthusiasts.

Our app is the solution to this challenge – bringing the complexity of NASA FITS files into easy-to-discover, user-friendly data. Users can quickly find real historical observations or surveys scans in the future without writing heavy code. Switch between various data layers on the fly, match targets with Gaia and WISE star catalogs and explore 102-channel infrared spectra in our Spectral Lab. Plus, our custom time-lapse slideshow allows you to observe the movement of the stars and changes in the space between dates in a smooth manner.

This is important because SPHEREx will observe the entire sky twice a year. SPHEREx Explorer transforms complex data into an easy-to-use, glowing space interface, smooth target syncing helps any one investigate cosmic history, search for ice in space, and watch the dynamic universe in action.
details: SPHEREx Explorer is a new use of deep space observation data, focusing on making it accessible with an easy to use and efficient web interface using React, Vite and Python FastAPI, and a specialised interface for NASA IRSA Multi-Extension FITS files. It is built to interact with live archive endpoints and survey predictions, making discovery simple and not requiring researchers or space enthusiasts to deal with heavy programming scripts. Users can switch between different data layers, overlay star catalogues Gaia and WISE onto their current view and decompose continuous near-infrared readings along all 102 spectral channels. The scans of historical surveys are also placed in fluid, movie-like time-lapses using the built-in time-line software, which is useful for monitoring the movement of stars and stellar variations. SPHEREx Explorer, combined with a glowing, glassmorphic command center showing synchronised targets from all over the world, is powerful astrophysics and simple design, making it accessible to all to study the history of the universe, investigate interstellar ices and explore the evolving universe.
